construct:517d64db16ceb6e6a692.name: natural_recovery_propensity
construct:517d64db16ceb6e6a692.description: Tendency for the original episode to remit or remain well without medication because of natural history, resilience, regression to the mean, and nonpharmacologic recovery.

construct:4cfc4a70f9d59a668364.name: past_escitalopram_response_tolerability
construct:4cfc4a70f9d59a668364.description: Historical symptom improvement, relapse prevention, side effects, and functional change while on escitalopram, reflecting drug effect plus natural recovery and expectancy.

construct:47ab45d6fa00e93be7ee.name: patient_taper_preference_beliefs
construct:47ab45d6fa00e93be7ee.description: Current motivation to taper or continue, perceived medication benefit, concerns about dependence or side effects, fear of relapse, and coping confidence.

construct:7b3d7a5f98ae353c60b6.name: taper_speed_dose_reduction
construct:7b3d7a5f98ae353c60b6.description: Rate and size of escitalopram dose reductions, including abrupt, linear, hyperbolic, paused, or reversed taper patterns.

construct:b7418d1841c57d53abf8.name: adherence_to_regimen
construct:b7418d1841c57d53abf8.description: Consistency with intended dose or taper plan, including missed doses, extra doses, and reinstatement behavior.

construct:27f64faaddd59b2ad491.name: escitalopram_dose_taken
construct:27f64faaddd59b2ad491.description: Actual escitalopram amount ingested at each model tick after taper instructions and adherence are realized.

construct:4a7b8d4d0772b0b10e4e.name: duration_current_escitalopram_use
construct:4a7b8d4d0772b0b10e4e.description: Length of continuous escitalopram use before taper decision, including time at stable maintenance dose.

construct:1ca8eec7961c69a0cbe1.name: stable_withdrawal_susceptibility
construct:1ca8eec7961c69a0cbe1.description: Stable person-specific susceptibility to SSRI discontinuation symptoms, distinct from the historical fact of prior withdrawal episodes.

construct:eb28b45b275c6732596f.name: neuroadaptation_dependence_state
construct:eb28b45b275c6732596f.description: Physiologic adaptation to sustained SSRI exposure that can make rapid reductions destabilizing even if the original disorder is inactive.

construct:2da513406663702e475d.name: withdrawal_symptom_burden
construct:2da513406663702e475d.description: Discontinuation symptoms after dose reduction, including dizziness, insomnia, anxiety, irritability, flu-like symptoms, nausea, and disequilibrium.

construct:ac82920bb78125ab0aca.name: external_stressful_events
construct:ac82920bb78125ab0aca.description: External shocks during follow-up such as loss, conflict, job strain, financial events, illness in others, or major schedule disruption.

construct:bb5a697c4e5f020f733d.name: perceived_stress_burden
construct:bb5a697c4e5f020f733d.description: Subjective stress load, threat appraisal, overload, uncontrollability, and daily hassles.

construct:07f8d9915eaa311c9e50.name: physical_activity
construct:07f8d9915eaa311c9e50.description: Amount and regularity of movement and exercise sufficient to affect sleep, reward, energy, and mood regulation.

construct:5bf588dc29d582cd7423.name: sleep_circadian_disruption
construct:5bf588dc29d582cd7423.description: Insomnia, hypersomnia, irregular sleep timing, circadian misalignment, and poor sleep quality.

construct:ecfbf689dbd8add308bb.name: clinical_monitoring_rescue_care
construct:ecfbf689dbd8add308bb.description: Frequency and quality of clinical follow-up, safety monitoring, medication review, dose rescue, and crisis support.

construct:428de2b75c12e36ca19d.name: other_psychotropic_or_somatic_treatments
construct:428de2b75c12e36ca19d.description: Concurrent medication changes, supplements, sleep aids, anxiolytics, stimulants, hormonal treatments, or somatic treatments affecting symptoms or exposure.

construct:6ca86c47aaf18b2472ce.name: internalizing_symptom_burden
construct:6ca86c47aaf18b2472ce.description: Primary outcome: latent depressive and anxiety symptom burden over the next two months, including mood, anhedonia, worry, irritability, somatic anxiety, and distress.

edge:f01776f0929a8eccc2fc.description: Underlying remission and relapse propensity changes symptom burden independently of the taper pathway.

edge:9f17859ba14225cbef18.description: Natural improvement can be misattributed to escitalopram if medication began during spontaneous improvement.

sources.title: Posternak and Miller (2001). Untreated short-term course of major depression.
sources.snippet: Wait-list studies show measurable spontaneous improvement over weeks.

edge:06d2e4026996e4b9379f.description: Perceived benefit and acceptable tolerability make extended use more likely.

edge:3d92787d7a5f9e0201a9.description: Perceived past benefit discourages tapering, while side effects or lack of perceived benefit encourage it.

edge:93cda69e8ea3105f7cde.description: Worsening symptoms can increase fear of tapering; wellness can increase confidence to taper.

edge:ffb1bdc7cf492b1d7f1d.description: Motivation, fear of relapse, and coping confidence affect how quickly the person attempts to reduce dose.

edge:027439d7acff15a9f7f3.description: Beliefs about benefit, harm, or dependence influence missed doses, self-directed dose changes, and reinstatement.

edge:66bd0e882b7fbd2118a1.description: Planned reductions mechanically lower the subsequent amount of escitalopram taken.

edge:14682ec416926f40197b.description: Missed doses, extra doses, and partial adherence change actual escitalopram dose relative to the plan.

sources.title: DiMatteo, Lepper, and Croghan (2000). Depression is a risk factor for noncompliance with medical treatment.
sources.snippet: Depression is associated with poorer adherence to medical regimens.

edge:c8efa1de930a894c06ce.description: Worsening depression or anxiety can reduce organization and motivation for taking medication as intended, or prompt rescue dosing.

sources.title: DiMatteo, Lepper, and Croghan (2000). Depression is a risk factor for noncompliance with medical treatment.
sources.snippet: Depressed patients were less likely to adhere to treatment recommendations.

edge:e41bd8d330491d104a1a.description: Withdrawal symptoms can lead to pausing the taper, reinstating, or taking rescue doses.

sources.title: Horowitz and Taylor (2019). Tapering of SSRI treatment to mitigate withdrawal symptoms.
sources.snippet: Withdrawal symptoms can motivate reinstatement and slower tapering.

edge:326df5ec6c9291a64dea.description: Discontinuation symptoms update beliefs about how risky or feasible tapering is.

edge:8b0771916792e703d7e9.description: Longer continuous exposure allows more physiologic adaptation to SSRI blockade.

sources.title: Horowitz and Taylor (2019). Tapering of SSRI treatment to mitigate withdrawal symptoms.
sources.snippet: Withdrawal risk is framed in relation to adaptation and nonlinear dose occupancy.

edge:73e5ab450d651575bcd5.description: Underlying discontinuation susceptibility causally affects current withdrawal burden, while prior history is treated as a marker and belief-shaper.

sources.title: Davies and Read (2019). A systematic review into antidepressant withdrawal effects.
sources.snippet: Withdrawal reactions are variable in incidence, duration, and severity.

edge:55e88b356c8e0a1a6eb2.description: Faster or larger dose reductions can precipitate withdrawal when physiologic adaptation and susceptibility are present.

edge:b3c79da49c3d691b8d84.description: Greater adaptation to chronic SSRI exposure increases susceptibility to symptoms when exposure falls.

sources.title: Davies and Read (2019). A systematic review into antidepressant withdrawal effects.
sources.snippet: Withdrawal reactions are reported by a substantial proportion of discontinuers.

edge:41f8d691f9ffb9121691.description: Discontinuation symptoms often include insomnia or disturbed sleep, which can worsen mood and anxiety.

sources.title: Davies and Read (2019). A systematic review into antidepressant withdrawal effects.
sources.snippet: Insomnia and related symptoms are among reported withdrawal effects.

edge:94b56531da4578528cca.description: Unpleasant or frightening withdrawal sensations increase threat appraisal and stress.

edge:0956802ffa3b8f7363c5.description: Withdrawal can directly raise anxiety, irritability, low mood, distress, and somatic symptoms.

sources.title: Lewis et al. (2021). Maintenance or Discontinuation of Antidepressants in Primary Care.
sources.snippet: Discontinuation increased relapse and withdrawal symptoms compared with maintenance.

edge:e96deda9a6084d6d4ed9.description: Actual dose changes the maintenance of antidepressant benefit and can alter subsequent internalizing symptom burden.

edge:6001378d624b64d8db27.description: External life events and demands increase perceived stress depending on appraisal and resources.

sources.title: Hammen (2005). Stress and depression.
sources.snippet: Stressful experiences are central precipitants and maintainers of depression.

edge:466eed55d5293ecb5f6a.description: Stress and arousal impair sleep onset, continuity, and circadian regularity.

edge:9df1507c29b9de944a33.description: Perceived overload and threat directly increase anxiety, dysphoria, irritability, and bodily arousal.

edge:00282e82c6e558b8219b.description: Regular physical activity improves sleep pressure, circadian stability, and sleep quality.

edge:0ffc13808e1300eb0e24.description: Exercise can directly improve mood, anxiety, energy, and self-efficacy.

sources.title: Schuch et al. (2016). Exercise as a treatment for depression.
sources.snippet: Physical exercise was associated with reduced depressive symptoms.

edge:347cf99a9951dfd01cf4.description: Poor sleep and circadian disruption worsen next-period mood, anxiety, irritability, energy, and concentration.

sources.title: Baglioni et al. (2011). Insomnia as a predictor of depression: a meta-analytic evaluation of longitudinal epidemiological studies.

edge:bc472e241b3651bc152a.description: Depression and anxiety can disturb sleep through worry, arousal, hypersomnia, irregular routines, and low activity.

edge:cbe7ea3961c0a9149ae2.description: Symptoms reduce energy, motivation, confidence, and routine, lowering subsequent physical activity.

edge:1198da260c8bcf398021.description: Severe discontinuation symptoms prompt clinician contact and potential taper modification.

edge:1d473931f0684c7749af.description: Worsening symptoms prompt more clinical contact, safety monitoring, and treatment adjustment.

edge:a3d943e0f5e7db74a977.description: Clinical contact can initiate or change adjunctive treatments for sleep, anxiety, mood, or medical contributors.

edge:2c2a94ecd60e62fa9f59.description: Other medication or somatic treatment changes can improve or worsen mood and anxiety independently of escitalopram tapering.

indicator:93c7007ff8e5a6565b25.name: phq9_screening_score
indicator:93c7007ff8e5a6565b25.how_to_measure: Use the `phq9_score` column directly when a PHQ-9 screening scale score is recorded. The score reflects depressive symptom burden over the prior two weeks ending at the visit date. Return null for support windows with no recorded PHQ-9 score.

indicator:b3eb347f05220d9f4130.name: gad7_screening_score
indicator:b3eb347f05220d9f4130.how_to_measure: Use the `gad7_score` column directly when a GAD-7 screening scale score is recorded. The score reflects anxiety symptom burden over the prior two weeks ending at the visit date. Return null for support windows with no recorded GAD-7 score.

indicator:b20fa3887689d5616a60.name: state_of_mind_valence
indicator:b20fa3887689d5616a60.how_to_measure: Use the `mood_valence` column directly from Apple State of Mind entries. Average all observed entries within the day. Higher valence means better mood and therefore less internalizing symptom burden.

indicator:8e1b73dd3c754b48e92c.name: journal_internalizing_symptom_severity
indicator:8e1b73dd3c754b48e92c.how_to_measure: Within each day, inspect `local_date`, `journal_text`, `imessage_text`, `mood_labels`, and `mood_associations` for first-person evidence of depressed mood, anhedonia, anxiety, worry, irritability, panic, somatic anxiety, hopelessness, guilt, or distress. Rate severity as none, mild, moderate, or severe based only on evidence in that day. Return `none` only when there is usable mood-related text or labels and they indicate no such symptoms; return null when there is no usable symptom evidence in the support window.

indicator:eca6b8b2c4379267b6c8.name: taper_speed_instruction_intensity
indicator:eca6b8b2c4379267b6c8.how_to_measure: Within each day, inspect `plan_text`, `clinical_note_text`, `medication_action`, `medication_name`, and `drug_name` for the escitalopram taper plan. Classify the intended reduction speed as none_or_continue, slow_or_paused_reduction, moderate_reduction, or rapid_stop_or_large_reduction. Return null if no escitalopram taper or continuation plan is documented in the support window.

indicator:eb0949a188790298c25d.name: escitalopram_documented_dose_mg
indicator:eb0949a188790298c25d.how_to_measure: Within each day, use medication rows where `medication_name` or `drug_name` contains escitalopram or Lexapro. Return the last non-null `medication_dose_mg` documented for escitalopram that day, in milligrams. Return null if no escitalopram dose is documented that day. This is a documented dose proxy, not proof of ingestion.

indicator:1f8878c9ba1ad571b89e.name: medication_adherence_documented
indicator:1f8878c9ba1ad571b89e.how_to_measure: Within each day, inspect `clinical_note_text`, `plan_text`, `journal_text`, and `imessage_text` for evidence about taking escitalopram as prescribed, missed doses, extra doses, self-directed changes, or reinstatement. Rate adherence as poor, partial, or consistent. Use `consistent` only when source evidence explicitly says the medication was taken as directed or no missed doses were reported in a medication-adherence context. Return null when there is no usable adherence evidence.

indicator:7a4890fc254d4a508b7c.name: sleep_efficiency_pct
indicator:7a4890fc254d4a508b7c.how_to_measure: Use the `sleep_efficiency_pct` column directly from Oura sleep periods. Average values over all sleep periods assigned to the day. Higher sleep efficiency indicates less sleep/circadian disruption.

indicator:21069529417a9a99ee50.name: daily_step_count
indicator:21069529417a9a99ee50.how_to_measure: Use the `step_count_count` column directly from Apple Health step count intervals. Sum all step counts within the day.

indicator:9becfedce394873f8c0c.name: journal_stress_severity
indicator:9becfedce394873f8c0c.how_to_measure: Within each day, inspect `journal_text`, `imessage_text`, `mood_labels`, and `mood_associations` for subjective stress, overwhelm, threat, uncontrollability, pressure, daily hassles, or feeling unable to cope. Rate as none, mild, moderate, or severe. Return `none` only when usable affect/stress evidence is present and indicates low or absent stress; return null if there is no usable evidence.

indicator:0b02f0d32a40caec29ef.name: external_stressor_event_count
indicator:0b02f0d32a40caec29ef.how_to_measure: Within each day, inspect `calendar_summary`, `calendar_description`, `journal_text`, `imessage_text`, `transaction_name`, `merchant_name`, `finance_category_primary`, and `finance_category_detailed` for external stressful events such as conflict, deadlines, job strain, illness in self/others, bereavement, financial shock, legal/administrative problems, travel disruption, or major schedule disruption. Count distinct stressful events in the day. Return 0 if there is usable daily source evidence and no stressful event is indicated; return null if no usable event/text/transaction evidence exists.

indicator:7f51bc663e8e0bbea95f.name: other_treatment_change_count
indicator:7f51bc663e8e0bbea95f.how_to_measure: Within each day, inspect `medication_name`, `drug_name`, `medication_dose_mg`, `medication_action`, `clinical_note_text`, `assessment_text`, and `plan_text` for non-escitalopram psychotropic medications, sleep aids, anxiolytics, stimulants, supplements, hormonal treatments, or somatic treatments that are initiated, stopped, increased, decreased, or used as needed. Count distinct non-escitalopram treatment changes or active PRN uses. Return 0 if medication/treatment evidence is present and no relevant non-escitalopram treatment is active or changed; return null if there is no usable treatment evidence.

indicator:c9a9156464b8dce5ba14.name: patient_taper_preference_level
indicator:c9a9156464b8dce5ba14.how_to_measure: Within each day, inspect `journal_text`, `imessage_text`, `clinical_note_text`, and `plan_text` for the patient's motivation to taper or continue escitalopram, perceived benefit, side-effect concerns, dependence concerns, fear of relapse, and coping confidence. Rate taper preference as wants_continue, ambivalent, prefers_slow_taper, or wants_stop_or_fast_taper. Return null if there is no usable preference/belief evidence.

indicator:a1c5e49b6b167636f7a0.name: natural_recovery_evidence_level
indicator:a1c5e49b6b167636f7a0.how_to_measure: Inspect `clinical_note_text`, `assessment_text`, `journal_text`, `mood_valence`, `phq9_score`, and `gad7_score` for evidence that symptoms improved or remained well during periods without medication change, through nonpharmacologic coping, stable life conditions, or spontaneous remission. Rate as low, moderate, or high. Return null if the available evidence cannot distinguish natural recovery or resilience from medication response.

indicator:cd5618fdf5311bf6e90d.name: past_escitalopram_response_tolerability_level
indicator:cd5618fdf5311bf6e90d.how_to_measure: Inspect `clinical_note_text`, `assessment_text`, `plan_text`, `journal_text`, medication fields, `phq9_score`, and `gad7_score` for historical improvement, relapse prevention, side effects, dose changes due to response/tolerability, or patient-reported benefit/harm while taking escitalopram. Rate net historical response/tolerability as poor_or_harmful, mixed_or_unclear, beneficial_with_side_effects, or clearly_beneficial_tolerated. Return null if no usable escitalopram response/tolerability history is available.

indicator:ea0f209a3393fba5194e.name: current_escitalopram_use_duration_proxy
indicator:ea0f209a3393fba5194e.how_to_measure: Use escitalopram-related `drug_name`, `medication_name`, `timestamp`, `local_date`, `days_supply`, `clinical_note_text`, and `plan_text` to estimate the length of continuous current escitalopram use before the taper decision. Prefer explicit duration statements in notes; otherwise use the span from first documented escitalopram record to the latest pre-taper escitalopram record when continuity is plausible from fills/notes. Return duration in days; return null if current-use duration cannot be estimated.

indicator:d14078f40ae3b26ae799.name: long_term_ssri_adaptation_proxy
indicator:d14078f40ae3b26ae799.how_to_measure: Within each day, inspect escitalopram-related `clinical_note_text`, `plan_text`, `medication_name`, `drug_name`, `medication_dose_mg`, `days_supply`, and `strength` for evidence of ongoing long-term escitalopram use or stable maintenance dosing. Rate adaptation proxy as none, short_or_uncertain, ongoing_maintenance, or long_term_maintenance. Return null if no escitalopram-use-duration or maintenance context is available in that day.

indicator:80833c21d9dd9f2ce5d5.name: clinical_contact_count
indicator:80833c21d9dd9f2ce5d5.how_to_measure: Count non-null `clinical_note_text` rows within each day. This measures clinical monitoring/contact volume. Return 0 when the day has rows from other sources but no clinical note; return null only if the support window has no rows at all.

indicator:a7234127c37d7ce4a0c2.name: rescue_or_monitoring_action
indicator:a7234127c37d7ce4a0c2.how_to_measure: Within each day, inspect `plan_text`, `clinical_note_text`, `medication_action`, `visit_type`, `department`, `calendar_summary`, and `calendar_description` for monitoring visits, follow-up plans, medication rescue, dose reinstatement, urgent care, crisis support, safety monitoring, or advice to pause/reverse taper. Return 1 if such monitoring or rescue care is documented, 0 if a relevant clinical/taper plan is present and no monitoring or rescue action is indicated, and null if there is no usable clinical or taper-care evidence.
